turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste either of our time. My son found out he got a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first.
So the defense is that he just types really fast?
I haven't said one word about typing, Hale. Owen doesn't need a defense; you need a basis. What do you have that's in writing, with a date on it?
182 words in six minutes. Wow. Maybe he should be a court stenographer.
Save the jokes for your students. "182 words in six minutes," measured how, on what day, and by whom? If there's a document behind that number, put it in front of me now.
I'm not here as anyone's counsel, Hale; I'm his mother. You've given me a number and two jokes, and no document. Show me something I can read, or I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
